**My thinking:**

I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life, since I was a teenager. My father grew wheat and corn, his father grew wheat and corn. That's what this flat, dry land is good for. I don't read much, but I know my soil, and I know what my neighbors do. Everyone here does the two-crop rotation — winter wheat goes in October, you harvest it in June, then you immediately plant summer corn in the same fields, harvest in September. That's the whole year.

I have about 10 mu of land. Not big, but it's mine.

For wheat, I'll buy improved variety seeds from the county seed station — the old seeds don't yield as well, and even I can see that. I put in base fertilizer before planting, urea and phosphate mixed in. In spring I top-dress more urea when the wheat starts jointing. Water matters a lot here — I pump groundwater from the tube well. I irrigate before winter sets in, again at jointing, again at heading. Three times at least. I spray herbicide in early spring, and if I see aphids before harvest I spray again. Plough the field before planting — I rent the tractor from the village service.

For corn, I plant right after wheat harvest, no time to waste. Hybrid seeds — everybody uses Xianyu or Zhengdan, they grow fast and yield well. I apply fertilizer at planting and again when the plant is knee-high. Summer rains usually help, but I'll irrigate once if July is dry. Minimal tillage — just rotary till the wheat stubble in.

I don't experiment. At 59, I stick to what works.
